 وَهَؤُلَاءِ الْمَلَاحِدَةُ فِي أَوَّلِ أَمْرِهِمْ يَنْفُونَ الصِّفَاتِ وَيَقُولُونَ:
 الْقُرْآنُ هُوَ اللَّهُ أَوْ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ.
 فَإِذَا قِيلَ لَهُمْ:
 غَيْرُ اللَّهِ.
 قَالُوا:
 فَغَيْرُ اللَّهِ مَخْلُوقٌ.
 وَفِي آخِرِ أَمْرِهِمْ يَقُولُونَ:
 مَا ثَمَّ مَوْجُودٌ غَيْرُ اللَّهِ أَوْ يَقُولُونَ الْعَالَمُ لَا هُوَ اللَّهُ وَلَا هُوَ غَيْرُهُ.
 وَيَقُولُونَ:
translated_text:
And although Allah Most High is the Creator of His servants’ acts, He does not describe Himself as those who perform these acts are described. He does not call Himself one who prays, fasts, eats or drinks. Glory be to Him! Exalted is He far above what the wrongdoers say.

As for the statement:

“There is no other,”

if the speaker means what the adherents of unity mean—namely, that nothing exists other than Allah—then this is outright unbelief.

If there were no other, He would not have said:

“Is it other than Allah I should take as a protector?”

Nor would He have said:

“Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?”

For they were ordering him to worship idols. If there were nothing other than Allah, His words would not have been valid:

“Is it other than Allah that you order me to worship, O ignorant ones?”

Nor would He have said:

“Then is it other than Allah I should seek as judge, when it is He who has sent down to you the Book, explained in detail?”

Nor would Abraham, Allah’s intimate friend, have said:

“Have you considered what you have been worshipping—you and your forefathers? Indeed, they are enemies to me, except the Lord of all worlds.”

Nor would he have said:

“Indeed, I am free of what you worship, except the One who created me; He will surely guide me.”

Abraham did not take his Lord as an enemy, nor did he disavow his Lord. If those gods whom they and their forefathers worshipped were not other than Allah, then Abraham would have disavowed Allah and taken Allah as an enemy. Far be it from Abraham to do such a thing!

These heretics initially deny the divine attributes and say:

“The Quran is either Allah or other than Allah.”

When they are told:

“Other than Allah,”

they say:

“Whatever is other than Allah is created.”

Yet ultimately they say:

“Nothing exists other than Allah.”

Or they say:

“The world is neither Allah nor other than Him.”

And they say:

original_text:
وَكُلُّ كَلَامٍ فِي الْوُجُودِ كَلَامُهُ سَوَاءٌ عَلَيْنَا نَثْرُهُ وَنِظَامُهُ فَيُنْكِرُونَ عَلَى أَهْلِ السُّنَّةِ إذَا أَثْبَتُوا الصِّفَاتِ وَلَمْ يُطْلِقُوا عَلَيْهَا اسْمَ الْغَيْرِ وَهُمْ لَا يُطْلِقُونَ عَلَى الْمَخْلُوقَاتِ اسْمَ الْغَيْرِ وَقَدْ سَمِعْت هَذَا التَّنَاقُضَ مِنْ مَشَايِخِهِمْ فَإِنَّهُمْ فِي ضَلَالٍ مُبِينٍ.
 وَأَمَّا قَوْل الشَّاعِرِ فِي شِعْرِهِ:
 أَنَا مَنْ أَهْوَى وَمَنْ أَهْوَى أَنَا؟
 وَقَوْلُهُ:
 إذَا كُنْت لَيْلَى وَلَيْلَى أَنَا.
 فَهَذَا إنَّمَا أَرَادَ بِهِ هَذَا الشَّاعِرُ الِاتِّحَادَ الْوَضْعِيَّ كَاتِّحَادِ أَحَدِ الْمُتَحَابَّيْنِ بِالْآخَرِ الَّذِي يُحِبُّ أَحَدُهُمَا مَا يُحِبُّ الْآخَرَ وَيُبْغِضُ مَا يُبْغِضُ وَيَقُولُ مِثْلَ مَا يَقُولُ وَيَفْعَلُ مِثْلَ مَا يَفْعَلُ وَهُوَ تَشَابُهٌ وَتَمَاثُلٌ لَا اتِّحَادُ الْعَيْنِ بِالْعَيْنِ إذْ كَانَ قَدْ اسْتَغْرَقَ فِي مَحْبُوبِهِ حَتَّى فَنِيَ بِهِ عَنْ رُؤْيَةِ نَفْسِهِ كَقَوْلِ الْآخَرِ:
 غِبْت بِك عَنِّي فَظَنَنْت أَنَّك أَنِّي فَإِمَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ غالطا مُسْتَغْرِقًا بِالْفَنَاءِ أَوْ يَكُونُ عَنَى التَّمَاثُلَ وَالتَّشَابُهَ وَاتِّحَادَ الْمَطْلُوبِ وَالْمَرْهُوبِ لَا الِاتِّحَادَ الذَّاتِيَّ. فَإِنْ أَرَادَ الِاتِّحَادَ الذَّاتِيَّ - مَعَ عَقْلِهِ لِمَا يَقُولُ - فَهُوَ كَاذِبٌ مُفْتَرٍ مُسْتَحِقٌّ لِعُقُوبَةِ الْمُفْتَرِينَ.
 وَأَمَّا قَوْل الْقَائِلِ:
 لَوْ رَأَى النَّاسُ الْحَقَّ لَمَا رَأَوْا عَابِدًا وَلَا مَعْبُودًا: فَهَذَا مِنْ جِنْسِ قَوْلِ الْمَلَاحِدَةِ الِاتِّحَادِيَّةِ الَّذِينَ لَا يُفَرِّقُونَ بَيْنَ الرَّبِّ وَالْعَبْدِ؛
translated_text:
“And every utterance in existence is His speech;
its prose and verse are all the same to us.”

They therefore object to the people of the Sunnah when they affirm the divine attributes without calling them “other than Allah,” yet they themselves do not call created things “other than Allah.” I have heard this contradiction from their own shaykhs. They are indeed in manifest error.

As for the poet’s words:

“I am the one I love, and the one I love is I?”

And his words:

“If I am Laylā and Laylā is I.”

The poet intended only union in the conventional sense, like the union between two lovers: each loves what the other loves, hates what the other hates, says what the other says, and does what the other does. This is similarity and likeness, not the union of one individual being with another. He had become so absorbed in his beloved that he lost awareness of himself, as another poet said:

“Absorbed in you, I lost sight of myself,
and thought that you were I.”

Either he is mistaken, overwhelmed by the loss of self-awareness, or he means similarity, likeness, and unity in what is sought and feared—not union of essences. If, however, he intends union of essences while understanding what he is saying, then he is a liar and fabricator who deserves the punishment of fabricators.

As for the statement:

“If people saw the Real, they would see neither a worshipper nor one worshipped,”

this is of the same kind as the statements of the heretical adherents of unity, who make no distinction between the Lord and the servant;

original_text:
وَقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ بَيَانُ قَوْلِ هَؤُلَاءِ وَهَؤُلَاءِ يَجْمَعُونَ بَيْنَ الضَّلَالِ وَالْغَيِّ بَيْنَ شَهَوَاتِ الْغَيِّ فِي بُطُونِهِمْ وَفُرُوجِهِمْ وَبَيْنَ مُضِلَّاتِ الْفِتَنِ.
 وَفِي الْحَدِيثِ عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ أَنَّهُ قَالَ:
 
{إنَّ أَخْوَفَ مَا أَخَافُ عَلَيْكُمْ شَهَوَاتِ الْغَيِّ فِي بُطُونِكُمْ وَفُرُوجِكُمْ}
 حَتَّى يَبْلُغَ الْأَمْرُ بِأَحَدِهِمْ إلَى أَنْ يَهْوَى المردان وَيَزْعُمُ أَنَّ الرَّبَّ تَعَالَى تَجَلَّى فِي أَحَدِهِمْ وَيَقُولُونَ: هُوَ الرَّاهِبُ فِي الصَّوْمَعَةِ؛ وَهَذِهِ مَظَاهِرُ الْجَمَالِ؛
 وَيُقَبِّلُ أَحَدُهُمْ الْأَمْرَدَ وَيَقُولُ:
 أَنْتَ اللَّهُ.
 وَيُذْكَرُ عَنْ بَعْضِهِمْ أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَأْتِي ابْنَهُ وَيَدَّعِي أَنَّهُ اللَّهُ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ أَوْ أَنَّهُ خَلَقَ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضَ وَيَقُولُ أَحَدُهُمْ لِجَلِيسِهِ:
 أَنْتَ خَلَقْت هَذَا وَأَنْتَ هُوَ وَأَمْثَالُ ذَلِكَ. فَقَبَّحَ اللَّهُ طَائِفَةً يَكُونُ إلَهُهَا الَّذِي تَعْبُدُهُ هُوَ مَوْطَؤُهَا الَّذِي تَفْتَرِشُهُ؛ وَعَلَيْهِمْ لَعْنَةُ اللَّهِ وَالْمَلَائِكَةِ وَالنَّاسِ أَجْمَعِينَ لَا يَقْبَلُ اللَّهُ مِنْهُمْ صَرْفًا وَلَا عَدْلًا.
 وَمَنْ قَالَ:
 إنَّ لِقَوْلِ هَؤُلَاءِ سِرًّا خَفِيًّا وَبَاطِنَ حَقٍّ وَإِنَّهُ مِنْ الْحَقَائِقِ الَّتِي لَا يَطَّلِعُ عَلَيْهَا إلَّا خَوَاصَّ خَوَاصِّ الْخَلْقِ: فَهُوَ أَحَدُ رَجُلَيْنِ - إمَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ مِنْ كِبَارِ الزَّنَادِقَةِ أَهْلِ الْإِلْحَادِ وَالْمَحَالِّ وَإِمَّا أَنْ يَكُونَ مِنْ كِبَارِ أَهْلِ الْجَهْلِ وَالضَّلَالِ. فَالزِّنْدِيقُ يَجِبُ قَتْلُهُ؛ وَالْجَاهِلُ يَعْرِفُ حَقِيقَةَ الْأَمْرِ فَإِنْ أَصَرَّ عَلَى هَذَا الِاعْتِقَادِ الْبَاطِلِ بَعْدَ قِيَامِ الْحُجَّةِ عَلَيْهِ وَجَبَ قَتْلُهُ.
translated_text:
and their views have already been explained. These people combine error with depravity: the depraved appetites of their bellies and sexual organs, together with trials that lead astray.

A hadith reports that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“What I fear most for you is the depraved appetites of your bellies and sexual organs.”

This can go so far that one of them becomes infatuated with beardless youths and claims that the Lord Most High has manifested Himself in one of them. They say, “He is the monk in the hermitage,” and, “These are manifestations of beauty.” One of them kisses a beardless youth and says, “You are Allah.”

It is reported that one of them used to have intercourse with his son and claim that he was Allah, Lord of all worlds, or that he had created the heavens and the earth. One of them says to his companion, “You created this, and you are He,” and other such things. May Allah disgrace a group whose god, whom they worship, is the very one with whom they have intercourse and whom they take to bed! Upon them is the curse of Allah, the angels, and all mankind. Allah will accept neither sarf nor ʿadl from them.

Anyone who says, “Their words contain a hidden secret and an inward truth, and this belongs to realities accessible only to the most select of the select among creation,” is one of two kinds of men: either one of the foremost heretics devoted to unbelief and al-mahāll, or one of the foremost people of ignorance and error. The heretic must be put to death. The ignorant person is to be informed of the true state of affairs; if he persists in this false belief after the proof has been established against him, he must be put to death.

original_text:
وَلَكِنْ لِقَوْلِهِمْ سِرٌّ خَفِيٌّ وَحَقِيقَةٌ بَاطِنَةٌ لَا يَعْرِفُهَا إلَّا خَوَاصُّ الْخَلْقِ. وَهَذَا السِّرُّ هُوَ أَشَدُّ كُفْرًا وَإِلْحَادًا مِنْ ظَاهِرِهِ؛ فَإِنَّ مَذْهَبَهُمْ فِيهِ دِقَّةٌ وَغُمُوضٌ وَخَفَاءٌ قَدْ لَا يَفْهَمُهُ كَثِيرٌ مِنْ النَّاسِ. وَلِهَذَا تَجِدُ كَثِيرًا مِنْ عَوَامِّ أَهْلِ الدِّينِ وَالْخَيْرِ وَالْعِبَادَةِ يُنْشِدُ قَصِيدَةَ ابْنِ الْفَارِضِ وَيَتَوَاجَدُ عَلَيْهَا وَيُعَظِّمُهَا ظَانًّا أَنَّهَا مِنْ كَلَامِ أَهْلِ التَّوْحِيدِ وَالْمَعْرِفَةِ وَهُوَ لَا يَفْهَمُهَا وَلَا يَفْهَمُ مُرَادَ قَائِلِهَا؛ وَكَذَلِكَ كَلَامُ هَؤُلَاءِ يَسْمَعُهُ طَوَائِفُ مِنْ الْمَشْهُورِينَ بِالْعِلْمِ وَالدِّينِ فَلَا يَفْهَمُونَ حَقِيقَتَهُ فَإِمَّا أَنْ يَتَوَقَّفُوا عَنْهُ أَوْ يُعَبِّرُوا عَنْ مَذْهَبِهِمْ بِعِبَارَةِ مَنْ لَمْ يَفْهَمْ حَقِيقَةً؛ وَإِمَّا أَنْ يُنْكِرُوهُ إنْكَارًا مُجْمَلًا مِنْ غَيْرِ مَعْرِفَةٍ بِحَقِيقَتِهِ وَنَحْوُ ذَلِكَ وَهَذَا حَالُ أَكْثَرِ الْخَلْقِ مَعَهُمْ.
 وَأَئِمَّتُهُمْ إذَا رَأَوْا مَنْ لَمْ يَفْهَمْ حَقِيقَةَ قَوْلِهِمْ طَمِعُوا فِيهِ وَقَالُوا:
 هَذَا مِنْ عُلَمَاءِ الرُّسُومِ وَأَهْلِ الظَّاهِرِ وَأَهْلِ الْقِشْرِ وَقَالُوا: عِلْمُنَا هَذَا لَا يُعْرَفُ إلَّا بِالْكَشْفِ وَالْمُشَاهَدَةِ وَهَذَا يَحْتَاجُ إلَى شُرُوطٍ وَقَالُوا: لَيْسَ هَذَا عُشُّك فَادْرُجْ عَنْهُ وَنَحْوُ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا فِيهِ تَعْظِيمٌ لَهُ وَتَشْوِيقٌ إلَيْهِ وَتَجْهِيلٌ لِمَنْ لَمْ يَصِلْ إلَيْهِ.
 وَإِنْ رَأَوْهُ عَارِفًا بِقَوْلِهِمْ نَسَبُوهُ إلَى أَنَّهُ مِنْهُمْ وَقَالُوا:
 هُوَ مِنْ كِبَارِ الْعَارِفِينَ.
translated_text:
But their words do have a hidden secret and an inward reality known only to the select among creation. This secret is even more steeped in unbelief and heresy than their outward meaning. Their doctrine contains subtleties, obscurities, and hidden meanings that many people may not understand. Thus, you find many ordinary people of religious devotion, goodness, and worship reciting Ibn al-Fārid’s poem, responding to it with displays of ecstasy, and venerating it, supposing that it expresses the words of people of monotheism and spiritual knowledge. Yet they understand neither the poem nor its author’s intent.

Likewise, groups of people renowned for learning and religious devotion hear these people’s words without understanding their true meaning. They may withhold judgment or describe their doctrine in terms that reflect a failure to understand its true nature. Alternatively, they may reject it in general terms without knowing what it really means, and so forth. This is how most people stand in relation to them.

When their leaders see someone who has not understood the true meaning of their doctrine, they see an opportunity in him and say:

“He is one of the scholars of outward forms, one of those concerned with outward appearances and mere husks.”

They say, “This knowledge of ours can be attained only through unveiling and direct witnessing, and this requires certain conditions.” They also say, “This is not your nest; move along,” and similar things that exalt this knowledge, arouse a longing for it, and portray anyone who has not attained it as ignorant.

If, however, they see that he understands their doctrine, they claim him as one of their own and say:

“He is one of the greatest masters of spiritual knowledge.”

original_text:
وَإِذَا أَظْهَرَ الْإِنْكَارَ عَلَيْهِمْ وَالتَّكْفِيرَ قَالُوا:
 هَذَا قَامَ بِوَصْفِ الْإِنْكَارِ لِتَكْمِيلِ الْمَرَاتِبِ وَالْمَجَالِي. وَهَكَذَا يَقُولُونَ فِي الْأَنْبِيَاءِ وَنَهْيِهِمْ عَنْ عِبَادَةِ الْأَصْنَامِ. وَهَذَا كُلُّهُ وَأَمْثَالُهُ مِمَّا رَأَيْته وَسَمِعْته مِنْهُمْ. فَضَلَالُهُمْ عَظِيمٌ وَإِفْكُهُمْ كَبِيرٌ وَتَلْبِيسُهُمْ شَدِيدٌ. وَاَللَّهُ تَعَالَى يُظْهِرُ مَا أَرْسَلَ بِهِ رَسُولَهُ مِنْ الْهُدَى وَدِينِ الْحَقِّ لِيُظْهِرَهُ عَلَى الدِّينِ كُلِّهِ وَكَفَى بِاَللَّهِ شَهِيدًا وَاَللَّهُ أَعْلَمُ.
translated_text:
And if he openly denounces them and declares them unbelievers, they say:

“He has assumed the role of one who objects, to complete the ranks and manifestations.”

They say the same about the prophets and their prohibition of idol worship. All this, and similar things, I have seen and heard from them. Their misguidance is immense, their lies grievous, and their deception profound. Allah Most High makes manifest the guidance and the religion of truth with which He sent His Messenger, to make it prevail over all religion. And sufficient is Allah as Witness. Allah knows best.

original_text:
فَصْلٌ:
فِيمَا عَلَيْهِ أَهْلُ الْعِلْمِ وَالْإِيمَانِ مِنْ الْأَوَّلِينَ والآخرين مِمَّا يُشْبِهُ الِاتِّحَادَ وَالْحُلُولَ الْبَاطِلَ وَهُوَ حَقّ - وَإِنْ سُمِّيَ حُلُولًا أَوْ اتِّحَادًا - وَهُوَ مَا عَلَيْهِ أَهْلُ الْإِسْلَامِ وَأَهْلُ السُّنَّةِ وَالْجَمَاعَةِ وَأَهْلُ الْمَعْرِفَةِ وَالْيَقِينِ مِنْ جَمِيعِ الطَّوَائِفِ بِدَلَالَةِ الْكِتَابِ وَالسُّنَّةِ.
 أَمَّا الْحُلُولُ:
 فَلَا رَيْبَ أَنَّ مَنْ عَلِمَ شَيْئًا فَلَا بُدَّ أَنْ يَبْقَى فِي قَلْبِهِ مِنْهُ أَثَرٌ وَنَعْتٌ وَلَيْسَ حَالُهُ بَعْدَ الْعِلْمِ بِهِ كَحَالِهِ قَبْلَ الْعِلْمِ بِهِ حَتَّى يَكُونَ الْعِلْمُ نِسْبَةً مَحْضَةً بِمَنْزِلَةِ الْعُلُوِّ وَالسُّفُولِ. فَإِنَّ الْمُسْتَعْلِيَ إذَا نَزَلَ زَالَ عُلُوُّهُ وَالسَّافِلَ إذَا اعْتَلَى زَالَ سُفُولُهُ وَالْعِلْمُ لَا يَزُولُ؛ بَلْ يَبْقَى أَثَرُهُ بِكُلِّ حَالٍ؛
 فَإِذَا كَانَ مَعَ الْعِلْمِ بِهِ يُحِبُّهُ أَوْ يَرْجُوهُ أَوْ يَخَافُهُ:
 كَانَ لِهَذِهِ الْأَحْوَالِ أَثَرٌ وَنَعْتٌ آخَرُ وَرَاءَ الْعِلْمِ وَالشُّعُورِ وَإِنْ كَانَا قَدْ يَتَلَازَمَانِ.
 فَإِذَا ذَكَرَهُ بِلِسَانِهِ:
 كَانَتْ هَذِهِ الْآثَارُ أَعْظَمَ.
 وَإِذَا خَضَعَ لَهُ بِسَائِرِ جَوَارِحِهِ:
 كَانَ ذَلِكَ أَعْظَمَ وَأَعْظَمَ. وَهَذِهِ الْمَعَانِي هِيَ فِي الْأَصْلِ مُشْتَرِكَةٌ فِي كُلِّ مُدْرِكٍ وَمُدْرَكٍ وَمُحِبٍّ وَمَحْبُوبٍ وَذَاكِرٍ وَمَذْكُورٍ وَسَوَاءٌ كَانَ عَلَى وَجْهِ الْعِبَادَةِ كَعِبَادَةِ اللَّهِ
translated_text:
Section

On what the people of knowledge and faith, both earlier and later, uphold, which resembles the false doctrines of union and indwelling but is true—even if it is called indwelling or union. This is what Muslims, the people of the Sunnah and the community, and those possessing knowledge and certainty among all groups uphold, as evidenced by the Quran and Sunnah.

As for indwelling:

There is no doubt that when someone knows something, an impression and a quality arising from it must remain in his heart. His state after knowing it is not the same as his state before knowing it, as though knowledge were merely a relation, like being above or below. Someone who is above ceases to be above when he descends, and someone who is below ceases to be below when he ascends. Knowledge, however, does not disappear; rather, its effect remains in every case.

If, in addition to knowing it, he loves it, looks to it with hope, or fears it, these states produce a further impression and quality beyond knowledge and awareness, although the two may go hand in hand.

If he mentions it with his tongue, these effects become greater.

If he submits to it with the rest of his bodily faculties, this becomes greater still. In principle, these meanings are common to every perceiver and object of perception, everyone who loves and the object of that love, and everyone who mentions something and what is mentioned—whether this takes the form of worship, such as worshipping Allah

وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ أَوْ عِبَادَةِ الْأَنْدَادِ مِنْ الَّذِينَ اتَّخَذُوا مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ أَنْدَادًا يُحِبُّونَهُمْ كَحُبِّ اللَّهِ أَوْ عَلَى غَيْرِ وَجْهِ الْعِبَادَةِ كَمُحِبِّ الْإِخْوَانِ وَالْوِلْدَانِ وَالنِّسْوَانِ وَالْأَوْطَانِ وَغَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِنْ الْأَكْوَانِ.
 فَالْمُؤْمِنُ الَّذِي آمَنَ بِاَللَّهِ بِقَلْبِهِ وَجَوَارِحِهِ إيمَانُهُ يَجْمَعُ بَيْنَ عِلْمِ قَلْبِهِ وَحَالِ قَلْبِهِ:
 تَصْدِيقُ الْقَلْبِ وَخُضُوعُ الْقَلْبِ وَيَجْمَعُ قَوْلَ لِسَانِهِ وَعَمَلَ جَوَارِحِهِ وَإِنْ كَانَ أَصْلُ الْإِيمَانِ هُوَ مَا فِي الْقَلْبِ أَوْ مَا فِي الْقَلْبِ وَاللِّسَانِ؛ فَلَا بُدَّ أَنْ يَكُونَ فِي قَلْبِهِ التَّصْدِيقُ بِاَللَّهِ وَالْإِسْلَامُ لَهُ هَذَا قَوْلُ قَلْبِهِ وَهَذَا عَمَلُ قَلْبِهِ وَهُوَ الْإِقْرَارُ بِاَللَّهِ. وَالْعِلْمُ قَبْلَ الْعَمَلِ وَالْإِدْرَاكُ قَبْلَ الْحَرَكَةِ وَالتَّصْدِيقُ قَبْلَ الْإِسْلَامِ وَالْمَعْرِفَةُ قَبْلَ الْمَحَبَّةِ وَإِنْ كَانَا يَتَلَازَمَانِ؛ لَكِنَّ عِلْمَ الْقَلْبِ مُوجِبٌ لِعَمَلِهِ مَا لَمْ يُوجَدْ مُعَارِضٌ رَاجِحٌ وَعَمَلُهُ يَسْتَلْزِمُ تَصْدِيقَهُ إذْ لَا تَكُونُ حَرَكَةً إرَادِيَّةً وَلَا مَحَبَّةً إلَّا عَنْ شُعُورٍ لَكِنْ قَدْ تَكُونُ الْحَرَكَةُ وَالْمَحَبَّةُ فِيهَا فَسَادٌ إذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ الشُّعُورُ وَالْإِدْرَاكُ صَحِيحًا.
 قَالَ عُمَرُ بْنُ عَبْدِ الْعَزِيزِ:
 
" مَنْ عَبَدَ اللَّهَ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ كَانَ مَا يُفْسِدُ أَكْثَرَ مِمَّا يُصْلِحُ "
 فَأَمَّا الْعَمَلُ الصَّالِحُ بِالْبَاطِنِ وَالظَّاهِرِ: فَلَا يَكُونُ إلَّا عَنْ عِلْمٍ وَلِهَذَا أَمَرَ اللَّهُ وَرَسُولُهُ بِعِبَادَةِ اللَّهِ وَالْإِنَابَةِ إلَيْهِ وَإِخْلَاصِ الدِّينِ لَهُ وَنَحْوِ ذَلِكَ فَإِنَّ هَذِهِ الْأَسْمَاءَ تَنْتَظِمُ الْعِلْمَ وَالْعَمَلَ جَمِيعًا: عِلْمَ الْقَلْبِ وَحَالَهُ وَإِنْ دَخَلَ فِي ذَلِكَ قَوْلُ اللِّسَانِ وَعَمَلُ الْجَوَارِحِ أَيْضًا فَإِنَّ وُجُودَ الْفُرُوعِ الصَّحِيحَةِ مُسْتَلْزِمٌ لِوُجُودِ الْأُصُولِ؛ وَهَذَا ظَاهِرٌ لَيْسَ الْغَرَضُ هُنَا بَسْطُهُ وَإِنَّمَا الْغَرَضُ

translated_text:
alone, with no partner, or worshipping rivals, as do those who take rivals besides Allah and love them as they love Allah; or takes a form other than worship, such as love for brothers, children, women, homelands, and other created things.

The faith of the believer who believes in Allah with his heart and bodily faculties encompasses both his heart’s knowledge and its state: the heart’s affirmation and submission. It also encompasses the words of his tongue and the actions of his bodily faculties. Although the foundation of faith is what is in the heart, or what is in the heart and on the tongue, his heart must affirm Allah and submit to Him. The former is the heart’s speech, and the latter is the heart’s action; this constitutes acknowledgment of Allah.

Knowledge precedes action, perception precedes movement, affirmation precedes submission, and knowledge precedes love, even though the two go hand in hand. Yet the heart’s knowledge necessarily gives rise to its action unless an opposing factor outweighs it, and its action entails its affirmation: neither voluntary movement nor love can arise without awareness. Movement and love, however, may be corrupt if awareness and perception are unsound.

Umar ibn Abd al-Azīz said:

“Whoever worships Allah without knowledge does more harm than good.”

As for righteous inward and outward action, it can arise only from knowledge. This is why Allah and His Messenger commanded worshipping Allah, turning to Him in repentance, devoting religion sincerely to Him, and similar things. These terms encompass both knowledge and action: the heart’s knowledge and its state, though the words of the tongue and the actions of the bodily faculties are also included. The presence of sound branches necessarily entails the presence of their roots. This is clear, and the purpose here is not to elaborate upon it; rather, the purpose is (1).

فَصْلٌ:
وَهُوَ أَنَّ الْمُؤْمِنَ لَا بُدَّ أَنْ يَقُومَ بِقَلْبِهِ مِنْ مَعْرِفَةِ اللَّهِ وَالْمَحَبَّةِ لَهُ:
 مَا يُوجِبُ أَنْ يَكُونَ لِلْمَعْرُوفِ الْمَحْبُوبِ فِي قَلْبِهِ مِنْ الْآثَارِ مَا يُشْبِهُ الْحُلُولَ مِنْ بَعْضِ الْوُجُوهِ لَا أَنَّهُ حُلُولُ ذَاتِ الْمَعْرُوفِ الْمَحْبُوبِ لَكِنْ هُوَ الْإِيمَانُ بِهِ وَمَعْرِفَةُ أَسْمَائِهِ وَصِفَاتِهِ. قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى. 
{نُورُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ مَثَلُ نُورِهِ كَمِشْكَاةٍ}
 الْآيَةَ قَالَ أبي بْنُ كَعْبٍ: 
" مَثَلُ نُورِهِ فِي قَلْبِ الْمُؤْمِنِ "
 فَهَذِهِ هِيَ الْأَنْوَارُ الَّتِي تَحْصُلُ فِي قُلُوبِ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ. وَقَدْ قِيلَ فِي قَوْله تَعَالَى 
{وَمَنْ يَكْفُرْ بِالْإِيمَانِ فَقَدْ حَبِطَ عَمَلُهُ}
 إنَّهُ الْكُفْرُ بِذَلِكَ؛
 فَإِنَّ مَنْ كَفَرَ بِالْإِقْرَارِ الَّذِي هُوَ التَّصْدِيقُ بِاَللَّهِ وَمَلَائِكَتِهِ وَكُتُبِهِ وَرُسُلِهِ وَالْإِسْلَامُ لَهُ:
 الْمُتَضَمِّنُ لِلِاعْتِقَادِ وَالِانْقِيَادِ لِإِيجَابِ الْوَاجِبَاتِ وَتَحْرِيمِ الْمُحَرَّمَاتِ وَإِبَاحَةِ الْمُبَاحَاتِ: فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ؛ إذْ الْمَقْصُودُ لَنَا مِنْ إنْزَالِ الْكُتُبِ وَإِرْسَالِ الرُّسُلِ هُوَ حُصُولُ الْإِيمَانِ لَنَا فَمَنْ كَفَرَ بِهَذَا فَهُوَ كَافِرٌ بِذَاكَ وَهَذَا قَدْ يُسَمَّى الْمَثَلَ وَالْمِثَالَ؛
 لِأَنَّهُ قَدْ يُقَالُ:
 إنَّ الْعِلْمَ مِثَالُ الْمَعْلُومِ فِي الْعَالَمِ وَكَذَلِكَ الْحُبُّ يَكُونُ فِيهِ تَمْثِيلُ الْمَحْبُوبِ فِي الْمُحِبِّ. ثُمَّ مِنْ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَدَّعِي أَنَّ كُلَّ عِلْمٍ وَكُلَّ حُبٍّ فَفِيهِ هَذَا الْمِثَالُ كَمَا يَقُولُهُ قَوْمٌ مِنْ الْمُتَفَلْسِفَةِ وَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يُنْكِرُ حُصُولَ شَيْءٍ مِنْ هَذَا الْمِثَالِ فِي شَيْءٍ مِنْ الْعِلْمِ وَالْحُبِّ.
 وَالتَّحْقِيقُ:
 أَنَّهُ قَدْ يَحْصُلُ تَمَثُّلٌ وَتَخَيُّلٌ لِبَعْضِ الْعَالِمِينَ وَالْمُحِبِّينَ حَتَّى
translated_text:
Section:

that the believer must have in his heart such knowledge of Allah and love for Him that the One he knows and loves leaves effects in his heart resembling indwelling in certain respects. This is not the indwelling of the very essence of the One known and loved; rather, it is faith in Him and knowledge of His names and attributes. Allah Most High says:

“The Light of the heavens and the earth. The likeness of His light is as a niche…”

—and so the verse continues. Ubayy ibn Kaʿb said:

“The likeness of His light in the believer’s heart.”

These, then, are the lights that arise in believers’ hearts. Concerning His words, Most High:

“Whoever rejects faith, his deeds have become worthless,”

it has been said that this refers to rejecting that faith. Whoever rejects acknowledgment—which consists of affirming Allah, His angels, His Books and His messengers, and submitting to Him, encompassing both belief and submission to the prescription of obligations, the prohibition of forbidden things and the permission of permissible things—is a disbeliever. For the intended benefit to us of the revelation of the Books and the sending of the messengers is that we attain faith. Whoever rejects this therefore rejects those.

This may be called a likeness and a representation, for it may be said that knowledge is a representation of what is known within the knower. Likewise, love involves a representation of the beloved within the lover. Some people claim that every instance of knowledge and love involves this representation, as some philosophers maintain. Others deny that any such representation arises in any instance of knowledge or love.

The precise conclusion is that mental representations and imagined images may arise in some who know and love, to the point that

they imagine the form of the beloved, though no sensory image may arise. This representation is not of the same kind as the reality itself at all. Rather, since knowledge corresponds to what is known and accords with it rather than contradicting it, there is a certain correspondence and resemblance between the two, and thus a kind of representation. An analogy is drawn between things because they share certain features; here, too, there is certainly some shared feature and some resemblance.

It has been said that this is what is meant by His words, Most High:

“There is nothing like Him,”

and His words:

“To Him belongs the highest description in the heavens and the earth.”

In a transmitted hadith:

“Neither My earth nor My heaven encompasses Me, but the heart of My believing servant—pure, pious, tranquil and tender—encompasses Me.”

It is also said: “The heart is the house of the Lord.” This is the servants’ share from their Lord and their portion of faith in Him. As one of the early Muslims is reported to have said:

“If any of you wishes to know his standing with Allah, let him consider Allah’s standing in his heart. For Allah accords the servant a standing with Him corresponding to the standing the servant accords Him in his heart.”

This has also been reported as traced back to the Prophet, through Ayyūb ibn Abd Allāh ibn Khālid ibn Safwān, from Jābir ibn Abd Allāh. It was transmitted by Abū Ya‘lā al-Mawsilī and by Ibn Abī al-Dunyā in The Book of Remembrance. For this reason, Jacob’s sons said:

“We worship your God and the God of your fathers, Abraham and Isaac.”

Their hearts’ devotion to Allah as God varies enormously in degree, increasing and decreasing. Their differences in this respect are so great that neither extreme can be precisely delimited. Indeed, it is established in an authentic report that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said concerning two men:

“This man is better than an earth full of men like that one.”

Thus, a single individual became

among humankind better than an earth full of his own kind; this is an immense disparity, the like of which does not occur among other animals.

This is the meaning indicated by the saying:

“Abū Bakr did not surpass you through greater prayer or fasting, but through something firmly settled in his heart.”

That is certainty and faith. Along the same lines are the words of the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace:

“I was weighed against the community and outweighed it; then Abū Bakr was weighed against the community and outweighed it; then Umar was weighed against the community and outweighed it; then the scales were raised.”

He also said, as reported from him by al-Siddīq:

“O people, ask Allah for certainty and well-being, for after certainty no one has been given anything better than well-being.”

This was transmitted by al-Tirmidhī, al-Nasā’ī in The Day and Night, and Ibn Mājah. Raqabah ibn Misqalah said to al-Sha‘bī:

“May Allah grant you the certainty in which alone souls find rest, and upon which alone one can rely in matters of religion.”

In Imam Ahmad’s Book of Asceticism, it is reported from [Sayyār, and Ja‘far narrated to us, from ‘Imrān al-Qasīr] (1), who said:

“Moses said, ‘My Lord, where may I find You?’

“He said, ‘O Moses, with those whose hearts are broken for My sake. I draw nearer to those hearts by a handspan each day; were it not for that, their hearts would burn up.’”

This meaning may be expressed more expansively, to the point that one says, “There is nothing in my heart but Allah; I have nothing but Allah.” Likewise, in the authentic hadith, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, reported that Allah, Mighty and Majestic, said:

“Did you not know that My servant so-and-so fell ill? Had you visited him, you would have found Me with him.”

And it is said:

“He dwells within the heart and fills it;
I do not forget Him and then recall Him.”

And it is said:

translated_text:
“Your image is before my eyes, your remembrance on my lips;
Your dwelling is within my heart—where, then, could you be absent?”

This state can grow immensely powerful, to the point that it is described as manifestation, unveiling, and the like, as all rational people agree. Along with it comes nearness to Him, as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The servant is nearest to his Lord when he is prostrating.”

And Allah Most High said in the divine hadith:

“Whoever draws near to Me by a handspan, I draw near to him by a cubit.”

But does the servant’s drawing near to Allah involve movement toward Allah, or toward certain places?

They agree that the servant’s body may move toward certain exalted places where faith in Allah is manifested through knowing Him, remembering Him, and worshipping Him—for example, by making pilgrimage to His House or going to His mosques. This includes Abraham’s words:

“Indeed, I am going to my Lord; He will guide me.”

As for the movement of his soul toward places such as the heavens and elsewhere, the majority of Muslims affirm it, while the Sabian Peripatetic philosophers and those who agree with them deny it. The movement of his soul or body toward Allah is affirmed by those of sound innate disposition and the adherents of the Sunnah and the community, but denied by many practitioners of speculative theology.

As for Allah’s nearness to His servant: does it follow the servant’s drawing near and being brought near—which consists in his knowledge or action—or is there another nearness on the Lord’s part? This is a matter of discussion, but this is not the place for it.

translated_text:
Those who affirm only the former hold two views concerning the Lord’s nearness. The first is that it consists in His manifesting Himself and becoming apparent to the servant. The second is that, in addition to this, it includes the servant’s approaching Him and drawing near through his deeds and movement. Nearness also has another meaning: similarity or correspondence, as when one says, “This closely resembles that.” This, however, is not the place to discuss it.

Section

As for what resembles union, two distinct entities cannot become one and the same entity, nor can their respective attributes become one and the same attribute, unless, after uniting, they are transformed into a third entity. This is like the union of water and milk: after uniting, they constitute a third thing, neither pure water nor pure milk.

For them to unite while each remains as it was before is impossible. From this, it is clear that Allah cannot unite with His creation, since His undergoing transformation is impossible. It is only causes and effects that are united in their particular object, while names and attributes are united in kind—as with two people at war with one another who are also intimate friends, one of whom comes to love exactly what the other loves, hate what he hates, take pleasure in what gives him pleasure, and suffer from what causes him suffering. This has innumerable levels and degrees; thus, their names and attributes have come to be of the same kind.

and the particular effects and causes associated with them—for example, the object of love or hatred—are one and the same, as with the Messenger whom all believers love. They are united in loving him in the sense that the one they love is the same, and one person’s love is of the same kind as another’s—not that they are the very same love. This concerns people’s union with one another: the brotherhood and intimate friendship of faith concerning which the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“The believers, in their mutual love, mercy, and compassion, are like a single body: when one limb suffers, the rest of the body responds with fever and sleeplessness.”

This is recorded in both Sahīh collections. Thus, one believer’s relationship to another is likened to that of one limb to another, both joined by a single soul.

For this reason, Allah refers to a fellow believer as one’s own self in several places in the Book and the Sunnah. He, Most High, said:

“So do not claim purity for yourselves.”

And He said:

“There has certainly come to you a Messenger from among yourselves.”

And He said:

“Allah has certainly bestowed His favour upon the believers by sending among them a Messenger from among themselves.”

And He said:

“So greet yourselves.”

And He said:

“So kill yourselves.”

When a believing servant turns to his Lord, worships Him, and acts in accord with Him, until he loves what his Lord loves, hates what his Lord hates, commands what his Lord commands, forbids what his Lord forbids, is pleased with what pleases his Lord, is angered by what angers his Lord, gives to those to whom his Lord gives, and withholds from those from whom his Lord withholds, he is the servant concerning whom the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, as reported by Abū Dāwūd through al-Qāsim from Abū Umāmah:

“Whoever loves for Allah’s sake and hates

for Allah’s sake, gives for Allah’s sake, and withholds for Allah’s sake has perfected his faith.” This servant’s religion has become wholly devoted to Allah, and he has fulfilled the worship for which he was created. Thus, the effects and causes of these attributes of his are united with the effects and causes of the Lord’s attributes. Servants attain this to varying degrees: if one is a prophet, he has a degree of accord with Allah that others do not; the messengers rank higher still, and the messengers of firm resolve higher yet. Our Prophet Muhammad, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, has the highest rank of nearness to Allah in every station. This accord is the permissible form of union, whether obligatory or recommended. It is concerning such things that the texts of the Book and the Sunnah speak.

Allah, Most High, said:

“Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you are actually pledging allegiance to Allah. The hand of Allah is over their hands.”

And He said:

“Allah and His Messenger are more worthy that they should please Him.”

And He, Most High, said:

“Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah.”

And He, Most High, said:

“Indeed, those who offend Allah and His Messenger.”

And He, Most High, said:

“Dearer to you than Allah and His Messenger.”

And He, Most High, said:

“Say, ‘The spoils belong to Allah and the Messenger.’”

The Messiah’s saying—if this wording is authentically reported from him—also falls into this category:

“I and my Father are one. Whoever has seen me has seen my Father.”

The same applies to similar sayings, for this resembles His saying, Most High:

“Indeed, those who pledge allegiance to you are actually pledging allegiance to Allah.”

And His saying:

“Whoever obeys the Messenger has indeed obeyed Allah.”

And other such expressions whose wording admits more than one interpretation.

translated_text:
Section

Something of this kind is also reported concerning the “friends of Allah,” who are the God-fearing. Al-Bukhārī narrated in his Sahīh from Abū Hurayra that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah Most High says: ‘Whoever shows hostility to a friend of Mine has challenged Me to war. Nothing by which My servant draws near to Me equals his fulfillment of what I have made obligatory upon him. My servant continues drawing near to Me through voluntary acts of worship until I love him. When I love him, I become his hearing with which he hears, his sight with which he sees, his hand with which he strikes, and his foot with which he walks. If he asks Me, I will surely give him; if he seeks My protection, I will surely protect him. I do not hesitate over anything I am to do as I hesitate over taking the soul of My believing servant: he dislikes death, and I dislike causing him distress, yet he must undergo it.’”

The first statement in the hadith is His saying:

“Whoever shows hostility to a friend of Mine has challenged Me to war.”

He thus makes hostility toward His servant who is His friend hostility toward Himself. His enemy and His servant’s enemy are one and the same, and hostility toward His friend is the very same hostility toward Him: these are not two distinct things. Yet Allah is not His servant, nor is the aspect of hostility toward His servant identical to the aspect of hostility toward Himself. Rather, the two coincide only in kind.

He then said:

“When I love him, I become his hearing, his sight, his hand, and his foot.”

In a narration outside the Sahīh, it reads:

“Through Me he hears, through Me he sees, through Me he strikes, and through Me he walks.”

Thus, His words:

translated_text:
“Through Me he hears, through Me he sees, through Me he strikes, and through Me he walks”

explain the meaning of His words:

“I become his hearing, his sight, his hand, and his foot.”

This does not mean that He becomes the very eyeball, fatty tissue, nerve, or foot. Rather, He remains the One sought through these organs and faculties, and in this respect He occupies their place. For the servant’s perception and movement depend upon his organs and faculties. When his perception and movement are through the True One, this does not refer to the creation of perception and movement, since that is common to those whom He loves and those whom He does not love. Rather, the beloved servant has his rightful share of this assistance from the True One, in proportion to his share in Allah’s being with His servants, His lordship, and His divinity; for each of these has both a general and a particular form.

In his Sahīh, Muslim narrates from Abū Hurayra that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Allah Most High says: ‘My servant, I was ill, but you did not visit Me.’ He replies: ‘My Lord, how could I visit You when You are the Lord of all worlds?’ He says: ‘Did you not know that My servant so-and-so was ill? Had you visited him, you would have found Me with him. My servant, I was hungry, but you did not feed Me.’ He replies: ‘My Lord, how could I feed You when You are the Lord of all worlds?’ He says: ‘Did you not know that My servant so-and-so was hungry? Had you fed him, you would have found that with Me.’”

In this hadith, He mentions the two true meanings, excludes the two false meanings, and explains them. His words:

“I was hungry and ill”

are language of union that affirms the true meaning. His words:

“You would have found Me with him, and you would have found that with Me”

deny identity of essence by excluding the false meaning, and affirm the distinction between the Lord and the servant.

translated_text:
And His words:

“You would have found Me with him”

are an expression denoting location. Each expression affirms the true meaning of true indwelling—through faith, not in essence—and explains His words:

“I was ill, but you did not visit Me.”

For if the Lord were identical with the sick person and the hungry person, then, upon visiting and feeding that person, one would have found Him to be that very person, and found that He had eaten the food.

There is a fine distinction between His words concerning the sick person:

“You would have found Me with him,”

and His words concerning the hungry person:

“You would have found that with Me.”

The sick person whom it is recommended to visit, and with whom one finds Allah, is the believer in his Lord who is in accord with his God and bound to Him in devoted friendship. As for the person receiving food, the wording may encompass every hungry person whom it is recommended to feed, for Allah says:

“Who is it that will lend Allah a good loan, so that He may multiply it for him many times over?”

Thus, anyone who gives obligatory or recommended charity has lent to Allah, glorified is He, through what he has given to His servant.

It is established in the Sahīh that the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“Whoever gives in charity the equivalent of a date from wholesome earnings—and Allah accepts only what is wholesome—Allah takes it in His right hand and nurtures it as one of you nurtures his foal or weaned camel calf, until it becomes like a mighty mountain.”

He also said:

“Charity indeed reaches the hand of the True One before it reaches the hand of the beggar.”

The more likely interpretation, however, is that the servant mentioned in connection with hunger is the same as the one mentioned in connection with illness: the servant who is Allah’s devoted ally, in whom there is a kind of union, even though Allah also rewards feeding an openly sinful person or a non-Muslim under Muslim protection.

A parallel to lending is giving support, as in the words of the Most High:

“And so that Allah may know who supports Him

and His messengers, though He is unseen,” and His words:

and similar passages. Support, however, involves a certain meaning; yet in such a case one does not say, “I was hungry.” Allah has mentioned lending and support in the Quran and attributed both to Himself: the former concerns provision, and the latter support. Visiting the sick is mentioned in the hadith. These three matters are mentioned in His words, Most High:

“and those who remain patient in poverty, hardship, and battle,”

and His words:

“They were afflicted by poverty and hardship and were shaken.”

The hadith concerns only poverty and hardship, because these are matters that the individual addressed in His words can attend to alone:

“My servant, I was ill and hungry.”

For this reason, He reproached him. Support, however, ordinarily requires a number of people, so generally no particular individual is reproached over it. Alternatively, the purpose of the hadith is to draw attention to these matters.

The Quran mentions support and provision, but not visiting the sick, because support and lending have a general scope and are not restricted to one person rather than another. Visiting the sick, however, is only for those with whom one finds the True One.

translated_text:
Section

These two meanings are sound and firmly established; indeed, they constitute the very essence of religion, certainty, and faith. The first—Allah being in a person’s heart through knowledge and love of Him—is obligatory upon everyone and indispensable to every believer. If he fulfills his obligation in this regard, he follows the middle course; if he neglects part of it, he wrongs himself; and if he abandons it entirely, he disbelieves in his Lord.

The second—being in accord with his Lord concerning what He loves and dislikes, what pleases Him and what angers Him—in its fullness belongs only to the foremost, those brought near to Allah. They draw near to Allah through voluntary acts of worship, which He loves but has not made obligatory, after fulfilling the obligations that He loves, requires, and punishes those who abandon.

Thus, when these people performed the inward and outward words and deeds beloved to the True One, encompassing knowledge, spiritual states, and burdens, Allah Most High loved them. He said:

“My servant continues to draw near to Me through voluntary acts of worship until I love him.”

They did what He loved, so He loved them. For recompense corresponds to the deed, bearing the same relationship to it as an effect bears to its cause.

It should not be imagined that this means the servant must perform every single action that Allah loves, for that is impossible. Rather, what is meant is that he should perform whatever inward and outward deeds he is capable of;

and he can perform more inward deeds than outward deeds, as one of the early generations said:

“The believer’s strength lies in his heart, and his weakness in his body; the hypocrite’s strength lies in his body, and his weakness in his heart.”

For this reason, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“A person will be with those he loves.”

He also said:

“There are men in Medina who have been with you on every journey you have made and in every valley you have crossed; a valid excuse kept them behind.”

He also said, “The two are equal in reward,” in the hadith concerning the person able to spend and the one unable to do so, who said, “If I had wealth like so-and-so’s, I would use it as he does.” Since their deeds of the heart were equal, and one of them had a valid excuse for being unable to act physically, their recompense was equal. As the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said:

“When a servant falls ill or travels, he is credited with deeds like those he used to perform when healthy and not travelling.”

original_text:
فَصْلٌ:
وَقَدْ يَقَعُ بَعْضُ مَنْ غَلَبَ عَلَيْهِ الْحَالُ فِي نَوْعٍ مِنْ الْحُلُولِ أَوْ الِاتِّحَادِ؛
 فَإِنَّ الِاتِّحَادَ فِيهِ حَقٌّ وَبَاطِلٌ لَكِنْ لَمَّا وَرَدَ عَلَيْهِ مَا غَيَّبَ عَقْلَهُ أَوْ أَفْنَاهُ عَمَّا سِوَى مَحْبُوبِهِ وَلَمْ يَكُنْ ذَلِكَ بِذَنْبِ مِنْهُ:
 كَانَ مَعْذُورًا غَيْرَ مُعَاقِبٍ عَلَيْهِ مَا دَامَ غَيْرَ عَاقِلٍ فَإِنَّ الْقَلَمَ رُفِعَ عَنْ الْمَجْنُونِ حَتَّى يُفِيقَ؛
 وَإِنْ كَانَ مُخْطِئًا فِي ذَلِكَ كَانَ دَاخِلًا فِي قَوْلِهِ:
 
{رَبَّنَا لَا تُؤَاخِذْنَا إنْ نَسِينَا أَوْ أَخْطَأْنَا}
 وَقَالَ: 
{وَلَيْسَ عَلَيْكُمْ جُنَاحٌ فِيمَا أَخْطَأْتُمْ بِهِ}
 . وَهَذَا كَمَا يُحْكَى أَنَّ رَجُلَيْنِ كَانَ أَحَدُهُمَا يُحِبُّ الْآخَرَ فَوَقَعَ الْمَحْبُوبُ فِي الْيَمِّ فَأَلْقَى الْآخَرُ نَفْسَهُ خَلْفَهُ.
 فَقَالَ:
 أَنَا وَقَعْت فَمَا الَّذِي أَوْقَعَك؟
 فَقَالَ:
 غِبْت بِك عَنِّي فَظَنَنْت أَنَّك أَنِّي. فَهَذِهِ الْحَالُ تَعْتَرِي كَثِيرًا مِنْ أَهْلِ الْمَحَبَّةِ وَالْإِرَادَةِ فِي جَانِبِ الْحَقِّ وَفِي غَيْرِ جَانِبِهِ وَإِنْ كَانَ فِيهَا نَقْصٌ وَخَطَأٌ فَإِنَّهُ يَغِيبُ بِمَحْبُوبِهِ عَنْ حُبِّهِ وَعَنْ نَفْسِهِ وَبِمَذْكُورِهِ عَنْ ذِكْرِهِ وَبِمَعْرُوفِهِ عَنْ عِرْفَانِهِ وَبِمَشْهُودِهِ عَنْ شُهُودِهِ وَبِمَوْجُودِهِ عَنْ وُجُودِهِ فَلَا يَشْعُرُ حِينَئِذٍ بِالتَّمْيِيزِ وَلَا بِوُجُودِهِ؛
 فَقَدْ يَقُولُ فِي هَذِهِ الْحَالِ:
 أَنَا الْحَقُّ أَوْ سُبْحَانِي أَوْ مَا فِي الْجُبَّةِ إلَّا اللَّهُ وَنَحْوَ ذَلِكَ وَهُوَ سَكْرَانُ بِوَجْدِ الْمَحَبَّةِ الَّذِي هُوَ لَذَّةٌ وَسُرُورٌ بِلَا تَمْيِيزٍ.
translated_text:
Section:

Some people who are overwhelmed by a spiritual state may fall into a form of divine indwelling or union. Union has both true and false senses. Yet when something comes upon a person that deprives him of reason or makes him oblivious to everything except his beloved, and this is not due to any sin on his part, he is excused and is not punished for it as long as he lacks reason. For an insane person is exempt from accountability until he regains his senses. Even if he is mistaken in this, he falls within His words:

“Our Lord, do not impose blame upon us if we have forgotten or erred.”

And He said:

“There is no blame on you for what you do by mistake.”

This resembles the story told of two men, one of whom loved the other. The beloved fell into the sea, and the other threw himself in after him. The first said, “I fell in, but what made you fall in?” He replied, “I became so absorbed in you that I lost awareness of myself, and thought that you were me.”

This state affects many of those devoted to love and spiritual aspiration, whether directed toward Allah or toward something else, although it involves deficiency and error. A person becomes so absorbed in his beloved that he loses awareness of his love and of himself; in the one he remembers, that he loses awareness of his remembrance; in the one he knows, that he loses awareness of his knowing; in the one he witnesses, that he loses awareness of his witnessing; and in the one whose presence he experiences, that he loses awareness of his own existence. At that point, he no longer perceives distinctions or his own existence.

In this state he may say, “I am the Truth,” “Glory be to me,” “There is nothing in this robe but Allah,” or similar things, while intoxicated by the ecstasy of love—a pleasure and joy unaccompanied by discernment.

original_text:
وَذَلِكَ السَّكْرَانُ:
 يُطْوَى وَلَا يُرْوَى إذَا لَمْ يَكُنْ سُكْرُهُ بِسَبَبِ مَحْظُورٍ.
 فَأَمَّا إذَا كَانَ السَّبَبُ مَحْظُورًا:
 لَمْ يَكُنْ السَّكْرَانُ مَعْذُورًا وَأَمَّا أَهْلُ الْحُلُولِ: فَمِنْهُمْ مَنْ يَغْلِبُ عَلَيْهِ شُهُودُ الْقَلْبِ وَتَجَلِّيه حَتَّى يَتَوَهَّمَ أَنَّهُ رَأَى اللَّهَ بِعَيْنَيْ رَأْسِهِ.
 وَلِهَذَا ذَكَرَ ذَلِكَ طَائِفَةٌ مِنْ الْعِبَادِ الْأَصِحَّاءِ غَلَطًا مِنْهُمْ وَقَدْ ثَبَتَ فِي صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ عَنْ النُّوَاسِ بْنِ سَمْعَانَ:
 
{أَنَّ النَّبِيَّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ لَمَّا ذَكَرَ الدَّجَّالَ وَدَعْوَاهُ الرُّبُوبِيَّةَ قَالَ: وَاعْلَمُوا أَنَّ أَحَدًا مِنْكُمْ لَنْ يَرَى رَبَّهُ حَتَّى يَمُوتَ}
 وَرُوِيَ هَذَا الْمَعْنَى عَنْ النَّبِيِّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ مِنْ وُجُوهٍ أُخْرَى مُتَعَدِّدَةٍ حَسَنَةٍ فِي حَدِيثِ الدَّجَّالِ.
 فَإِنَّهُ لَمَّا ادَّعَى الرُّبُوبِيَّةَ ذَكَرَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فُرْقَانَيْنِ ظَاهِرَيْنِ لِكُلِّ أَحَدٍ أَحَدُهُمَا:
 أَنَّهُ أَعْوَرُ وَاَللَّهُ لَيْسَ بِأَعْوَرَ الثَّانِي: أَنَّ أَحَدًا مِنَّا لَنْ يَرَى رَبَّهُ حَتَّى يَمُوتَ وَهَذَا إنَّمَا ذَكَرَهُ فِي الدَّجَّالِ مَعَ كَوْنِهِ كَافِرًا؛ لِأَنَّهُ يَظْهَرُ عَلَيْهِ مِنْ الْخَوَارِقِ الَّتِي تُقَوِّي الشُّبْهَةَ فِي قُلُوبِ الْعَامَّةِ.
translated_text:
As for someone in this state of intoxication, his utterances should be passed over, not repeated, provided that his intoxication was not caused by something prohibited. If its cause was prohibited, however, he is not excused.

Among those who hold to divine indwelling are some who become so overwhelmed by the heart’s witnessing and the manifestation it experiences that they imagine they have seen Allah with their physical eyes. This is why some otherwise sound worshippers have mistakenly reported such an experience. It is authentically reported in Sahīh Muslim from al-Nawwās ibn Sam‘ān:

“When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, spoke of the Dajjāl and his claim to lordship, he said: ‘Know that none of you will see his Lord until he dies.’”

The same meaning has also been reported from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, through several other sound chains of transmission in accounts concerning the Dajjāl.

When the Dajjāl claimed lordship, the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, mentioned two distinguishing signs evident to everyone. The first is that the Dajjāl is blind in one eye, whereas Allah is not blind in one eye. The second is that none of us will see his Lord until he dies. He mentioned this specifically concerning the Dajjāl, despite his being a disbeliever, because extraordinary feats occur at his hands that strengthen the misleading impression in the hearts of ordinary people.

original_text:
فَصْلٌ:
فَإِذَا عُرِفَ الِاتِّحَادُ الْمُعَيَّنُ مِمَّا يُشْبِهُ الْحُلُولَ أَوْ الِاتِّحَادَ الَّذِي فِيهِ نَوْعُ حَقٍّ تَبَيَّنَ أَيْضًا مَا فِي الْمُطْلَقِ مِنْ ذَلِكَ.
 فَنَقُولُ:
 لَا رَيْبَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ رَبُّ الْعَالَمِينَ رَبُّ السَّمَوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِينَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَرَبُّ الْعَرْشِ الْعَظِيمِ رَبُّ الْمَشْرِقِ وَالْمَغْرِبِ لَا إلَهَ إلَّا هُوَ فَاِتَّخِذْهُ وَكِيلًا رَبُّكُمْ وَرَبُّ آبَائِكُمْ الْأَوَّلِينَ رَبُّ النَّاسِ مَلِكُ النَّاسِ إلَهُ النَّاسِ. وَهُوَ خَالِقُ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَكِيلٌ خَلَقَ الزَّوْجَيْنِ الذَّكَرَ وَالْأُنْثَى مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ إذَا تُمْنَى. وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَمَلِيكُهُ وَهُوَ مَالِكُ الْمُلْكِ؛ يُؤْتِي الْمُلْكَ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيَنْزِعُ الْمُلْكَ مِمَّنْ يَشَاءُ وَيُعِزُّ مَنْ يَشَاءُ وَيُذِلُّ مَنْ يَشَاءُ بِيَدِهِ الْخَيْرُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ لَهُ مَا فِي السَّمَوَاتِ وَمَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا وَمَا تَحْتَ الثَّرَى الرَّحْمَنُ عَلَى الْعَرْشِ اسْتَوَى لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ 
{مَا مِنْ دَابَّةٍ إلَّا هُوَ آخِذٌ بِنَاصِيَتِهَا إنَّ رَبِّي عَلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ}
 . قُلُوبُ الْعِبَادِ وَنَوَاصِيهِمْ بِيَدِهِ وَمَا مِنْ قَلْبٍ إلَّا وَهُوَ بَيْنَ إصْبَعَيْنِ مِنْ أَصَابِعِ الرَّحْمَنِ إنْ شَاءَ أَنْ يُقِيمَهُ أَقَامَهُ وَإِنْ شَاءَ أَنْ يُزِيغَهُ أَزَاغَهُ. وَهُوَ الَّذِي
translated_text:
Section

Once particular union has been understood, including what resembles indwelling or a union containing an element of truth, the corresponding issues concerning absolute union also become clear.

We therefore say:

There is no doubt that Allah is the Lord of all worlds, the Lord of the heavens and the earths and all that lies between them, and the Lord of the Mighty Throne; the Lord of the East and the West—there is no deity but Him, so take Him as your Trustee; your Lord and the Lord of your forefathers; the Lord of mankind, the King of mankind, the God of mankind.

He is the Creator of all things, and He is the Trustee over all things. He created the two sexes, male and female, from a sperm-drop when emitted. He is the Lord and Sovereign of everything, and the Owner of all dominion. He grants dominion to whom He wills and takes dominion away from whom He wills; He honours whom He wills and abases whom He wills. All good is in His hand, and He has power over all things.

To Him belongs whatever is in the heavens, whatever is on earth, whatever lies between them, and whatever is beneath the soil. The Most Merciful rose over the Throne. To Him belongs all dominion, and to Him belongs all praise, and He has power over all things.

“There is no creature but that He holds it by its forelock. Indeed, my Lord is on a straight path.”

The hearts and forelocks of His servants are in His hand. There is no heart except that it is between two fingers of the Most Merciful. If He wills to set it aright, He sets it aright; and if He wills to cause it to deviate, He causes it to deviate. And He is the One who

causes laughter and weeping and grants wealth and possessions. He is the One who sends the winds as heralds of His mercy and sends down water from the sky, reviving the earth after its death and spreading throughout it creatures of every kind. He is

“the One who created the heavens and the earth and made darkness and light; yet those who disbelieve equate others with their Lord.”

“Whoever Allah wills to guide, He opens his heart to Islam; and whoever He wills to lead astray, He makes his heart tight and constricted, as though he were climbing into the sky. Thus Allah places defilement upon those who do not believe.”

“He is Allah; there is no deity except Him. To Him belongs all praise in this life and the Hereafter. His is the judgement, and to Him you will be returned.”

He is the Ever-Living, the Sustainer of all, whom neither drowsiness nor sleep overtakes. He upholds justice and watches over every soul and what it earns. He is the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner.

“There is no creature on earth whose provision does not rest with Allah.”

What Allah has willed! There is no power except through Allah. Whatever Allah wills comes to pass, and whatever He does not will does not come to pass. There is neither might nor power except through Allah, and there is no refuge from Him except with Him.

These meanings, and others like them, concern His Lordship, sovereignty, creation, provision, guidance, aid, beneficence, kindness, governance and workmanship. Connected with these is the fact that He knows all things and has power over all things, and that He is All-Hearing, All-Seeing. Hearing one thing does not distract Him from hearing another; requests do not confound Him, nor does He grow weary of those who persist in their pleas. He sees the black ant crawling across a solid rock in the darkness of night.

All of this is true, and it is the pure affirmation of His oneness in His Lordship. Along with this, He has given each thing its form and then guided it; He has made everything He created excellent and began the creation of man from clay.

original_text:
وَهَذَا صُنْعُ اللَّهِ الَّذِي أَتْقَنَ كُلَّ شَيْءٍ وَالْخَيْرُ كُلُّهُ بِيَدَيْهِ وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ الرَّاحِمِينَ وَهُوَ أَرْحَمُ بِعِبَادِهِ مِنْ الْوَالِدَةِ بِوَلَدِهَا كَمَا أَقْسَمَ عَلَى ذَلِكَ النَّبِيُّ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ وَسَلَّمَ فَقَالَ:
 
{وَاَللَّهِ لَلَّهُ أَرْحَمُ بِعِبَادِهِ مِنْ هَذِهِ الْوَالِدَةِ بِوَلَدِهَا}
 إلَى نَحْوِ هَذِهِ الْمَعَانِي الَّتِي تَقْتَضِي شُمُولَ حِكْمَتِهِ وَإِتْقَانَهُ وَإِحْسَانَهُ خَلْقَ كُلِّ شَيْءٍ وَسِعَةَ رَحْمَتِهِ وَعَظَمَتِهَا وَأَنَّهَا سَبَقَتْ غَضَبَهُ كُلُّ هَذَا حَقٌّ.
 فَهَذَانِ الْأَصْلَانِ عُمُومُ خَلْقِهِ وَرُبُوبِيَّتِهِ وَعُمُومُ إحْسَانِهِ وَحِكْمَتِهِ:
 أَصْلَانِ عَظِيمَانِ وَإِنْ كَانَ مِنْ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَكْفُرُ بِبَعْضِ الْأَوَّلِ كَالْقَدَرِيَّةِ الَّذِينَ يُخْرِجُونَ أَفْعَالَ الْعِبَادِ عَنْ خَلْقِهِ وَيُضِيفُونَهَا إلَى مَحْضِ فِعْلِ ذِي الِاخْتِيَارِ أَوْ الطَّبِيعَةِ الَّذِينَ يَقْطَعُونَ إضَافَةَ الْفِعْلِ إلَى اللَّهِ سُبْحَانَهُ وَيُضِيفُونَهُ إمَّا إلَى الطَّبْعِ أَوْ إلَى جِسْمٍ فِيهِ طَبْعٌ أَوْ إلَى فَلَكٍ أَوْ إلَى نَفْسٍ أَوْ غَيْرِ ذَلِكَ مِمَّا هُوَ مِنْ مَخْلُوقَاتِهِ الْعَاجِزَةِ عَنْ إقَامَةِ نَفْسِهَا فَهِيَ عَنْ إقَامَةِ غَيْرِهَا أَعْجَزُ. وَمِنْ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَجْحَدُ بَعْضَ الثَّانِي أَوْ يُعْرِضُ عَنْهُ مُتَوَهِّمًا خُلُوَّ شَيْءٍ مِنْ مَخْلُوقَاتِهِ عَنْ إحْسَانِ خَلْقِهِ وَإِتْقَانِهِ وَعَنْ حِكْمَتِهِ وَيَظُنُّ قُصُورَ رَحْمَتِهِ. وَعَجْزِهَا مِنْ الْقَدَرِيَّةِ الإبليسية أَوْ الْمَجُوسِيَّةِ وَغَيْرِهِمْ.
 وَإِذَا كَانَ كَذَلِكَ:
 فَجَمِيعُ الْكَائِنَاتِ: آيَاتٌ لَهُ شَاهِدَةٌ دَالَّةٌ مُظْهِرَةٌ لِمَا هُوَ مُسْتَحِقٌّ لَهُ مِنْ الْأَسْمَاءِ الْحُسْنَى وَالصِّفَاتِ الْعُلَى؛ وَعَنْ مُقْتَضَى أَسْمَائِهِ وَصِفَاتِهِ خَلَقَ الْكَائِنَاتِ. فَإِنَّ الرَّحِمَ شُجْنَةٌ مِنْ الرَّحْمَنِ خَلَقَ الرَّحِمَ وَشَقَّ لَهَا مِنْ اسْمِهِ؛ وَهُوَ الرَّازِقُ
translated_text:
and this is the workmanship of Allah, who has perfected everything. All good is in His two hands. He is the Most Merciful of those who show mercy, and He is more merciful to His servants than a mother is to her child, as the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, affirmed with an oath:

“By Allah, Allah is more merciful to His servants than this mother is to her child.”

These and similar meanings affirm His all-encompassing wisdom, the perfection and excellence with which He created everything, and the vastness and greatness of His mercy, which precedes His wrath. All of this is true.

These two principles—the all-encompassing nature of His creation and Lordship, and the all-encompassing nature of His beneficence and wisdom—are two great principles. Yet some people disbelieve in part of the first, such as the Qadariyyah, who exclude human actions from His creation and attribute them solely to the action of an agent endowed with choice; or those who appeal to nature, who sever the attribution of action to Allah, glorified is He, and attribute it instead to an inherent nature, a body endowed with such a nature, a celestial sphere, a soul, or some other created thing. These creatures cannot sustain themselves and are even less capable of sustaining anything else.

Others deny part of the second principle or turn away from it, imagining that some of His creatures lack the excellence and perfection of His workmanship and His wisdom, and supposing His mercy to be limited and powerless. These include the Iblīs-like or Magian Qadariyyah and others.

Since this is so, all existing things are signs of Him: they bear witness to, indicate and reveal the most beautiful names and exalted attributes that rightfully belong to Him. He created all existing things in accordance with what His names and attributes entail. Thus, the tie of kinship (rahim) is a bond stemming from the All-Merciful (al-Rahmān): He created the tie of kinship and derived its name from His own; and He is the Provider

, the Possessor of Power, the Ever-Firm, who provides for whomever He wills without measure. He is the Guide and Helper: He guides whomever He wills to a straight path and helps His messengers and those who believe, both in this worldly life and on the Day when the witnesses rise. He is the All-Wise, the All-Knowing, the Merciful, who has made manifest effects of His knowledge, wisdom, and mercy that none but He can enumerate.

He is the Lord of all worlds, and the worlds are filled with the effects of His names and attributes. Everything glorifies Him with praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Some people, through knowledge and understanding, perceive the indications and testimony these things contain. Those whose hearing Allah opens hear the mountains and birds repeating His praises and understand the speech of birds.

If His manifestation and self-disclosure are interpreted in this sense, this is correct. However, the terms “manifestation” and “self-disclosure” are ambiguous, as we shall explain, if Allah Most High wills.

If someone says, “I have never seen anything without seeing Allah before it,” because He is its Lord, and the Lord precedes the servant; or, “I saw Allah after it,” because it is His sign, evidence pointing to Him, and a witness to Him, and knowledge of what is indicated follows knowledge of the evidence; or, “I saw Allah in it,” meaning that the effects of the Maker are manifest in His handiwork—then this is correct.

Indeed, the entire Quran explains this and points to it. This is the religion of the messengers and the path of those whom Allah has blessed: the prophets, the steadfastly truthful, the martyrs, and the righteous. It is the belief of the Muslims who belong to Ahl al-Sunnah wa-l-Jamāʿah, and of those included among them: people of knowledge and faith, endowed with understanding and certainty—the pious allies of Allah.

Section:
Errors in This Matter

Many of those who turn toward Allah, when they devote themselves to remembering Him, worshipping Him, and returning to Him in repentance, perceive in their hearts this all-embracing lordship and this encompassing of all things. For He encompasses everything, and He—glorified be He—is the Truth who created the heavens and the earth. Among His signs is that the heaven and the earth stand by His command. The sun, the moon, and the stars are subjected to His command. Surely, creation and command belong to Him. He created the heavens and the earth and everything between them only for a true purpose. He—glorified be He—is the Light of the heavens and the earth:

“Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The parable of His light is that of a niche containing a lamp”—to the end of the verse.

With Him—glorified be He—there is neither night nor day. The light of the heavens comes from the light of His Face. This is what ‘Abd Allāh ibn Mas‘ūd said.

“He does not sleep, nor is it fitting for Him to sleep. He lowers and raises the balance. The deeds of the night are raised to Him before the deeds of the day, and the deeds of the day before the deeds of the night. His veil is light—or fire. Were He to remove it, the radiance of His Face would burn everything in His creation that His sight reaches.”

This is what the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said in the hadith reported by both al-Bukhārī and Muslim, narrated by Abū Mūsā.

فَقَدْ يَشْهَدُ الْعَبْدُ الْقَدْرَ الْمُشْتَرَكَ بَيْنَ الْمَصْنُوعَاتِ وَهُوَ الْحَقُّ الْمَوْجُودُ فِيهَا الَّذِي هُوَ شَامِلٌ لَهَا فَيَظُنُّ أَنَّهُ الْخَالِقُ لِمُطَابَقَتِهِ لَهُ فِي نَوْعٍ مِنْ الْعُمُومِ وَإِنَّمَا هُوَ صُنْعُهُ وَخَلْقُهُ ثُمَّ قَدْ يَرْتَقِي إلَى حِجَابٍ مِنْ حُجُبِهِ النُّورِيَّةِ أَوْ النَّارِيَّةِ فَيَظُنُّ أَنَّهُ هُوَ ثُمَّ يَرْتَقِي إلَى نُورِهِ وَمَا يَظْهَرُ مِنْ أَثَرِ صِفَاتِهِ؛ فَقَدْ يَقَعُ بَعْضُ هَؤُلَاءِ فِي نَحْوٍ مَنْ مَذْهَبِ أَهْلِ الِاتِّحَادِ الْمُطْلَقِ الْعَامِّ؛

translated_text:
Thus, a servant may perceive the element common to created things—the reality present in them and encompassing them—and suppose that it is the Creator, because it resembles Him in being universal in a certain respect. Yet it is only His handiwork and creation. He may then ascend to one of His veils of light or fire and suppose that it is He, then ascend to His light and the manifest effects of His attributes. Some of these people may thus fall into something akin to the doctrine of absolute, universal union of Creator and creation.

But if Allah comes to their aid in His mercy, and they hold fast to the rope of Allah and follow His guidance, they realize that all this is created by Allah, that the Creator is not the creation, and that they are all servants of Allah.

Sometimes this may happen to someone in a state of loss of self-awareness or spiritual intoxication. He is then mistaken and in error, although this is forgiven him if it arises from a cause that is not prohibited, as we have mentioned in the analogous case of union with a particular individual.

Section

Just as he witnesses His lordship, His all-encompassing governance of the world, His wisdom and His mercy, so too does he witness His universal divinity. For He is the One who is God in heaven and God on earth—God in heaven and God on earth.

“All who are in the heavens and the earth ask of Him; every day He is engaged in a matter.”

Likewise, His words:

“And He is Allah in the heavens and on the earth.”

This verse is understood according to one of the two interpretations, following those who pause at His words, “and on the earth.” The meaning is that He is Allah in the heavens and Allah on earth; there is none in either who is Allah other than Him. Although this resembles His words:

“And He is the One who is God in heaven and God on earth,”

it is more emphatic. A comparable statement is His saying:

“Had there been gods in them other than Allah, both would have fallen into ruin.”

He has also said:

“To Him belongs the highest attribute in the heavens and the earth, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.”

And He, exalted is He, has said:

“The seven heavens, the earth, and all who are in them glorify Him. There is not a thing that does not glorify Him with praise, but you do not understand their glorification.”

And He has said:

“Do they seek a religion other than Allah’s, when all who are in the heavens and the earth have submitted to Him, willingly or unwillingly, and to Him they will be returned?”

And His words, exalted is He:

“To Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, as do their shadows in the mornings

and the evenings.” And His words:

“Have you not seen that to Allah prostrates whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on earth, as do the sun, the moon, the stars, the mountains, the trees, the animals, and many people?”

And His words, exalted is He:

“To Him belongs whoever is in the heavens and the earth; all are obedient to Him.”

“And He is the One who originates creation, then repeats it, and that is easier for Him. To Him belongs the highest attribute in the heavens and the earth.”

And His words:

“Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on earth glorifies Allah, and He is the Almighty, the All-Wise.”

“Whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on earth glorifies Allah, the Sovereign, the Most Holy, the Almighty, the All-Wise.”

These and similar passages express His divinity, the humility and submission of created beings before Him, their need for Him, their requests of Him, and creation’s invocation of Him—through worship, through petition, or through both together.

As for those who turn away from Him when free to choose:

“When harm touches you at sea, all those you invoke vanish except Him.”

“Who answers the distressed when he calls upon Him?”

We witness that every object of worship other than Him, from His Throne to the depths of His earth, is false, except His noble Face. Just as we witness that all created things depend on Him for their beginning, we witness that they depend on Him for their end; otherwise, they would be without reality. These are the meanings that express created beings’ worship of Him and their attachment to Him.

These meanings, together with the earlier meanings expressing His lordship over them and His creation of them, require us to recognize that He is the Lord of mankind, the Sovereign of mankind, the God of mankind, and the Lord of all worlds. There is no god but Him. Created beings possess nothing of themselves; rather, they are pure nonexistence and utter negation. Whatever existence they possess is from Him and through Him.

original_text: ثُمَّ إنَّهُ إلَيْهِ مَصِيرُهَا وَمَرْجِعُهَا؛ وَهُوَ مَعْبُودُهَا وَإِلَهُهَا لَا يَصْلُحُ أَنْ يُعْبَدَ إلَّا هُوَ كَمَا لَمْ يَخْلُقْهَا إلَّا هُوَ لِمَا هُوَ مُسْتَحِقُّهُ بِنَفْسِهِ وَمُتَفَرِّدٌ بِهِ مِنْ نُعُوتِ الْإِلَهِيَّةِ الَّتِي لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ فِيهَا وَلَا سُمِّيَ لَهُ وَلَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ. فَهُوَ الْأَوَّلُ الَّذِي لَيْسَ قَبْلَهُ شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ الْآخِرُ الَّذِي لَيْسَ بَعْدَهُ شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ الظَّاهِرُ الَّذِي لَيْسَ فَوْقَهُ شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ الْبَاطِنُ الَّذِي لَيْسَ دُونَهُ شَيْءٌ وَهُوَ مَعَنَا أَيْنَمَا كُنَّا وَنَعْلَمُ أَنَّ مَعِيَّتَهُ مَعَ عِبَادِهِ عَلَى أَنْوَاعٍ وَهُمْ فِيهَا دَرَجَاتٌ. وَكَذَلِكَ رُبُوبِيَّتُهُ لَهُمْ وَعُبُودِيَّتُهُمْ الَّتِي هُمْ بِهَا مُعَبَّدُونَ لَهُ وَكَذَلِكَ أُلُوهِيَّتُهُمْ إيَّاهُ وَأُلُوهِيَّتُهُ لَهُمْ وَعِبَادَتُهُمْ الَّتِي هُمْ بِهَا عَابِدُونَ وَكَذَلِكَ قُرْبُهُ مِنْهُمْ وَقُرْبُهُمْ مِنْهُ.
translated_text:
Moreover, their final destination and return are to Him. He is their object of worship and their God. None but Him is worthy of worship, just as none but Him created them, because of the attributes of divinity that are His by right and His alone. He has no partner in these attributes, no peer, and nothing is like Him.

He is the First, before whom there is nothing; the Last, after whom there is nothing; the Outward, above whom there is nothing; and the Inward, nearer than whom there is nothing. He is with us wherever we are. We know that His being with His servants takes various forms, and that they occupy different degrees in this regard.

The same applies to His lordship over them and their servitude, through which they are made subject to Him; to their taking Him as their God, His being their God, and their worship, through which they are worshippers; and likewise to His nearness to them and their nearness to Him.

translated_text:
Section

This, then, concerns what resembles union or indwelling in a particular individual, such as a prophet, a righteous man, or someone similar. We have explained what it contains of pure truth and of truth mingled with falsehood. Allah willing, we shall explain what it contains of pure falsehood.

This category occurs only in someone who worships Allah, glorified is He, and is devoted to Him, or who is thought to do so. Through this, Allah’s divinity becomes manifest in His servant, as do the servant’s turning to his Lord and his concordance with Him in what He loves and approves, commands and forbids.

Another category may be confused with this: the effects of His lordship that the Lord manifests in some of His servants, even though this is neither something He has commanded nor an act of worship of Him. Examples include the share of His dominion and authority that He grants to certain rulers invested with power, who may or may not be Muslims, such as Pharaoh, Genghis Khan, and others like them; the provision and wealth He bestows upon some of His servants; and the beauty He apportions to some of His servants, both men and women. Likewise, there is the knowledge and understanding He bestows, the states He grants, or what He gives him

translated_text:
of extraordinary phenomena, including various forms of unveiling and influence, whether these people are believers or unbelievers, such as the one-eyed Dajjāl and others like him. In this category, the effects of lordship and the workings of divine power are more manifest in a particular servant than in others, just as the effects of divinity and the prescriptions of religious law are more manifest in those belonging to the first category than in others.

Both categories may come together in a servant, as they do in the angels, prophets, and allies of Allah, such as our Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and the Messiah, son of Mary, and others. This category alone suffices with respect to the effects of the creative words, just as the first category does with respect to the effects of the religious words. For events occur only through Allah’s will and power.

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, would seek and take refuge in Allah’s perfect words, beyond which neither the righteous nor the wicked can pass, and would instruct others to seek refuge in them. Neither the righteous nor the wicked can escape the words by which Allah brought all things into being. Thus, no dominion, authority, wealth, beauty, knowledge, state, unveiling, or exercise of influence exists except through His will, His power, and His perfect words. Yet some of this is beloved to Allah and commanded by Him, while some is hated by Allah and forbidden—rather, permissible or pardoned.

Since it occurs through Allah’s will, power, and word, and none but He has the power to bring it about, it is attributed to Allah with respect to His lordship and dominion. It therefore shares enough common ground and resemblance with the first category that some people have erred concerning Allah’s command, treating it as one and the same in both categories.

translated_text:
Worse still, they also erred concerning the Lord Himself, equating some of the servants held in subjection in the second category with some of the worshipping servants in the first. Through this confusion, they embraced the doctrines of union and indwelling, to the point that some worshipped Pharaoh and the Dajjāl, while others worshipped beautiful forms and the like, claiming that these were manifestations of beauty. These people rejected worship and faith at times, and the One worshipped at others.

Since our purpose here is to explain the truth of these matters, or whatever truth they contain, we have mentioned this.

As for the first: Allah, glorified be He, has distinguished, through the Quran and faith, between His religious command and His creation of all that exists. Allah, glorified be He, is the Creator, Lord, and Sovereign of everything, including all beings, their attributes, and their actions. Whatever Allah wills comes to pass, and whatever He does not will does not come to pass. Nothing falls outside His will, and nothing occurs except by His will.

Some of this has been denied by the Magian Qadariyya, both within this community and outside it. They claim that Allah did not create the actions of His servants—angels, jinn, human beings, and animals—and that He cannot bestow any more good upon His servants than He has already bestowed upon them. Indeed, they claim that He has no power over their actions, and thus is not powerful over all things; or that evil deeds occur contrary to His will and intent. They are misguided innovators who oppose the Quran, the Sunnah, the consensus of the early generations of this community, and what is known through reason and experience.
